messages:
jessica: Heads up — several customers reporting API p99 spikes and occasional 504s for generate endpoints from us-east -> eu-west paths, started ~2026-03-17 06:15 UTC. Seeing 3-4x p99 on completions. cc @oncall-bot

oncall-bot: Alert: metric api.request.p99 for model/gptx-prod in path us-east1->eu-west spiked above threshold at 06:16 UTC. Incident ID: INC-20260317-01

mike: Can you paste a sample request id or a quick traceroute? is it customer traffic or internal synthetic?

jessica: Customer ticket CID-98721 attached. They reported TLS handshake delays (~200-400ms) before request body. I grabbed a quick curl and openssl output: `curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'` -> `0.210 0.620 1.020`

Also snippet: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -msg -brief` showed multiple TLS Retransmit msgs and long client_hello->server_hello intervals.

ravi: I ran `mtr -r -c 8 eu-west-edge-1` from our probe nodes. Observed intermittent extra hop via transit-ix-3 (us-east2) adding ~75-110ms. Some probes resolved dns -> eu-west-edge-2, others -> eu-west-edge-6, TTLs low. Looks like DNS rotation + transit route flip.

olivia: We deployed a routing weight experiment at 04:30 UTC to shift low-priority traffic for capacity tests. @zach any chance that leaked into prod?

zach: I did a canary shift in bgp weights for testing. It should have been scoped, but I see an incomplete isolate rule pushed to the global policy at 04:28 — rolling it back now. Sorry team.

mike: While zach rolls back, we should apply a quick mitigation for the affected customer org (cust-org-558): set region affinity to prefer us-east1 to keep them on stable path. Command: `redwoodctl routing set-affinity --org cust-org-558 --prefer-region us-east1 --ttl 3600`

jessica: Support asked for repro steps to send to customer. Drafting: 1) Run `curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'` 2) If TLS delay >200ms, capture `tcpdump -ni any port 443 -c 200 -w /tmp/tls-slow.pcap` 3) Run `dig api.redwood.ai +short` several times and record IP rotation/TLS endpoint geography.

oncall-bot: Rollback of bgp weight policy detected at 06:38 UTC. Change ID: CHG-20260317-459. Monitoring metrics.

ravi: Post-rollback numbers: p95 back near baseline, p99 improved from 1.2s to ~0.65s but still noisy. Traces show DNS sometimes returning a mixed set of A records that point to different POPs; client picks one and then gets hairpin via transit. Need DNS-level affinity and CDN pinning.

olivia: Agreed. Follow-ups: 1) Add a short-term DNS TTL pinning for critical customers 2) Audit routing feature gating so test shifts can't modify global policy 3) Create synthetic probe to detect mixed-pop A sets and alert 4) Support to offer affected customers a small credit. I'll file a postmortem ticket.

support: I sent an interim status update to the customer and offered a credit for impacted 06:15-06:45 window. Customer acknowledged and will re-test tomorrow morning.

jessica: Thanks. Zack's rollback and affinity change mitigated immediate pain. Leaving monitoring on for next 24h. If p99 stays > 2x baseline we'll reopen. :thumbsup:

mike: Also let's instrument TLS handshake timing in our ingestion traces (client_hello->server_hello) so we can alert on handshake regressions next time.

olivia: Opening RFC for stricter deploy isolation and a quick ops playbook for routing experiments.

jessica: Closing thread once metrics remain stable for two hours. Great job moving fast.
